claim: Dr Anthony Fauci wrote a paper regarding the Spanish Flu and stated that the majority of deaths in 1918-1919 was because of bacterial pneumonia from wearing masks.
doc: Research published in The Journal of Infectious Diseases found that most victims of the 1918–1919 influenza pandemic succumbed to bacterial pneumonia following influenza virus infection, rather than to the virus acting alone. The pneumonia occurred when bacteria that normally inhabit the nose and throat invaded the lungs along a pathway created when the virus destroyed cells lining the bronchial tubes and lungs. NIAID Director Anthony Fauci stated: "The virus landed the first blow while bacteria delivered the knockout punch." Pathologist Jeffery Taubenberger examined lung tissue from 58 soldiers who died in 1918 and 1919, finding evidence ranging from primary viral pneumonia to severe secondary bacterial pneumonia. Medical experts agree that bacteria, not influenza viruses, were the greatest cause of death during the 1918 pandemic, and Dr Fauci's publication made no claim that masks caused flu deaths.

claim: India's imports from China increased by 27% during the period April-August 2020.
doc: India's imports from China declined sharply in 2020. From January to February 2020, India's imports from China were as low as US$9.5 billion, reflecting a 12.4 per cent trade decline in the initial two months of COVID-19. Imports fell to a record low of USD 3.2 billion in both April and May 2020, coinciding with pandemic-induced lockdowns, before recovering to USD 4.8 billion in June and USD 5.6 billion in July—nearly back to the pre-lockdown level of USD 5.8 billion in March. For the first seven months of 2020, India's imports from China totalled USD 32.2 billion, still down 24.7% year-on-year. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal confirmed that imports from China declined by 27.63% during April–August 2020.

normalized_claim: Between 2010 and 2018, the Uighur population had the region’s highest birthrate, at about 12 newborns per 1,000 people in Xinjiang, China.
claim: Between 2010 and 2018, the Uighur population had the region’s highest birthrate, at about 12 newborns per 1,000 people in Xinjiang, China.
doc: The Uyghur population is concentrated in the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region of northwest China, with approximately 10 million Uyghurs in China and at least 300,000 in Central Asian republics. The birthrate for Uyghurs in Xinjiang dropped from 14.85 per 1,000 in 2010 to 10.69 per 1,000 in 2018. In the predominantly Uyghur prefectures of Kashgar and Hotan, yearly birthrates between 2010 and 2018 ranged from 24.27 to 8.17 per 1,000, with an overall average of approximately 16+ and a 2018 figure of 8.17. Birth rates in Hotan and Kashgar plunged more than 60% from 2015 to 2018, compared to a 24% drop across Xinjiang and just 4.2% nationwide. The Uyghur birth rate of about 12 per 1,000 does not match official data from Xinjiang Statistical Yearbooks, and the 2018 figure for Hotan and Kashgar was below both regional and national averages. Researchers attribute the dramatic decline to a birth control campaign involving sterilisations, IUDs, and mandatory birth control measures.
label: False

perturb_type2_False: Between two thousand and fifteen and two thousand and twenty-three, the Uighur population had the region’s highest birthrate, at about thirteen newborns per one thousand, one hundred people in Xinjiang, China.
